purpose: Engine profile for DamIT Hazard (damit:classify). DamIT Hazard reads every threshold, label, scenario, modifier and preset from the Appendix A files of this catalog (methods, scenarios, modifiers, labels, presets) and translates them to its classifier. This file holds only what those files do not express: the receptor-type vocabulary of Hazard's layers, which TM-11 chart applies to which receptor, sampling defaults, and a few Hazard-specific engine switches; preset status marks, the USBR M1 reading and New York's R2 / R8 variants live in presets.json and modifiers.json so DamIT Screener reads them too. It must never repeat a value that the other files carry (a test enforces this).
disclaimer_lead: Informational screening aid, not legal or engineering advice and not a regulatory determination.
disclaimer_tail: Rules change: the current statutes, rules and agency guidance control. Items marked (unverified) or (secondary) should be confirmed before a preset is relied on, and every suggestion still needs an engineer's review.

general.base_class_note: With no hit the suggestion is the lowest consequence class (Low). Minimal / Very Low / No Public Hazard need an engineer's call (no method returns ordinal 0).
general.wet_min_depth_note: Plugin default: any depth above this counts as inundated (Appendix A: 'inundated at any depth').
general.sampling_note: Sampling defaults copied from DamSafety_Hazard (constants.OSM_EDGE_BUFFER_FT = 5 ft edge ring around an outline, DEFAULT_POINT_RADIUS_FT = 20 ft disc around a point, LINE_SAMPLE_STEP_FT = 10 ft along roads and rail). Not from the source document; editable.

receptor_types.structure_type_map_note: Hazard receptor type -> catalog structure_type. A catalog structure_types list (e.g. M2) is expanded to every Hazard type that maps to one of its entries.
receptor_types.road_class_map_note: Catalog road_class -> Hazard road_class where the names differ.

charts.names_note: Catalog TM-11 chart name -> chart key in damit_hazard/data/tm11_charts.json (the digitized curves stay in DamIT Hazard).

verification_legend.verified: Confirmed against a primary or official source in the source document (unmarked statements).
verification_legend.secondary: Only a secondary source was found (source document label: Secondary).
verification_legend.unverified: Not confirmed; carried for reference only (source document label: Unverified).
verification_legend.draft: The governing guidance is itself marked DRAFT.

params.chart_for_type_note: Which chart applies to which receptor type is a plugin default (TM-11 names the charts: houses on foundations, mobile homes, passenger vehicles, adults, children); edit it per study.

params.rows_note: High at high_depth_ft or more at the row's high datum, or DV high_dv or more; otherwise Low below low_below_ft (a low_below_ft of 0 means at or below the datum: below the foundation ground line), else Significant; Unoccupied farm or storage buildings: Low when flow is above the foundation line. Walkout basements may use walkout_high_depth_ft in place of the home row's high depth where occupants can move upstairs (walkout_option).

M3.row_params_note: Which catalog M3 parameter (or which catalog rule's depth literal, *_rule) fills each cell of Hazard's M3 rows. datum_rule / high_datum_rule name the catalog rule whose depth field sets the row's datum for the Significant / Low split and for the High test (institutions: foundation for the split, lowest floor for High).

M8c.note: The catalog writes 'main_highway_4lane' as a road class; Hazard reads a lanes attribute and treats this many lanes or more on a main highway as that class.

params.high_outage_note: 'Several weeks' is not a number in the source; set high_outage_days per study or mark major_population on the lifeline.

params.auto_map_note: auto_map is a DamIT Hazard default that guesses an M13 descriptor (catalog low/significant/high_kinds vocabulary) from the receptor type, keyed by the M13 wording: 'general' (catalog default) or the preset's M13 variant. A guessed descriptor is advisory; a home in the general wording is guessed as 'isolated_home' (Significant), a lower bound: serious damage to homes is High, and an engineer decides.

params.near_margin_note: The source gives no borderline margin; set near_margin_ft to promote M1 points within that depth below the high-danger line.

variants.storage_limit: No breach model and storage at or over the limit (or unknown): a class below High is not justified → High.
variants.lowering_from_high: Current class High and the analysis is not TM-11-based unsteady modeling: the class is not lowered.

variants.general: Receptors with transient occupancy are left out of the life-safety methods.
variants.incidental: People only incidentally present (walking on the dam, driving lightly traveled roads, recreating outside an established area) are left out.
variants.three_part_test: Loss of life is unlikely only if people are temporary, there are no residences or overnight campsites, and the owner controls access and keeps an EAP with a warning process; otherwise transients are not left out.

USBR.notes: S5 for borderline dams is (unverified). TM-11 Figs 4–6 (vehicles, adults, children) are not digitized in this plugin: M1 flags those receptors.

BIA.notes: BIA's 1–6 Significant rule is from FEMA P-919 (July 2012): (secondary). No scenario confirmed: fall back to M13 and engineering judgment.

ND.notes: N.D. Admin. Code § 89-08-01-01; DWR policy REG_05.2026 effective April 1, 2026 (superseded REG_05.2024a). 'Significant' means the same as 'Medium'. The ND Dam Design Handbook was not reviewed.

R5.basis: approved plans, permits or active construction

NE.notes: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 46-1601 et seq.; Title 458. Minimal is generally limited to farm pond dams (engineer's call).

NY.notes: Class D (defunct dam) is an administrative status and is left out. Sunny-day and rainy-day breaches: the most severe governs.

VA.notes: Significant may cause loss of life. Significant dams of 50,000 ac-ft or more held to the High SDF is (unverified) and not used here. M5 is the incremental-analysis variant: it supports lowering a proposed class only.

ID.notes: 2 ft or more at residences is sufficient (not the only reason) for High. Pre-2023 versions used a 2 ft / 2 fps test (not used).

CO.notes: Rule 4.13 sunny-day failure, reservoir full to the high water line (Rule 4.14). The Rule 4.15 Hydrologic Hazard sizes spillways and is not covered.

RI.notes: Scenario depends on the current class (§ 1.9(B)). The Director evaluates Low and Significant dams at least every 10 years.

AZ.notes: Classification regardless of the dam's condition. Very Low needs an engineer's call.

R5.basis: zoning and development projected over 10 years

CA.notes: Extremely High for critical facilities is case by case. DWR's older 'considerable loss of life' wording is superseded by the regulation.

presets_note: Per-preset refinements DamIT Hazard needs that presets.json does not carry: notes, R5 basis wording and California's 'S1 or S2' choice. Keys are preset IDs or aliases. Preset status (NRCS unverified, NY draft), the USBR M1 'marks lives, returns no class' reading and New York's R2 floor presumption and R8 lowering-from-High variant are in presets.json, where DamIT Screener reads them as well.
